_note: Provisioning profiles for `malign cloud launch --profile NAME`. A profile is the machine SHAPE plus the package floors that a run needs. It exists because provisioning was retyped each time and the floors were remembered rather than declared -- transformers cannot read .bin checkpoints under torch<2.6, and that floor silently cost the July grid 13 models.

default.description: One A100 80GB, the shape every twp/grid run has used.

pin_reasons.torch>=2.6: transformers refuses .bin checkpoints under torch<2.6 (CVE-driven torch.load policy). Thirteen models failed to load in the July grid on exactly this and it read as a model problem, not an environment one. See project_torch_bin_floor.

bigdisk.description: Same card, 600 GB. For rosters whose cumulative download exceeds the default disk when --purge is not used.

ssm.description: For SSM/Mamba AND hybrid (Falcon-H1) models. **THE KERNELS ARE NOT OPTIONAL FOR HYBRIDS: MEASURED 19.3x ON Falcon-H1-7B, 2026-08-03** (0.0670 -> 1.2933 cells/s on the twp loop, A100, bf16; 21.4 h -> 1.1 h for 5,166 cells). CORRECTION TO THIS FIELD'S PREVIOUS TEXT, which said kernels gave NO speedup and reasoned that twp re-runs the full sequence per tree node so the scan kernel is not binding. THE MEASUREMENT BEHIND THAT WAS SOUND AND THE GENERALISATION WAS NOT: it was taken on Falcon3-Mamba-7B, a PURE SSM (0.62-0.64 with kernels vs 0.61-0.72 without), and was quoted twice to predict no speedup for Falcon-H1, a HYBRID. Wrong by 19x. **A PRIOR TESTED ON ONE MEMBER OF A CLASS IS NOT A FACT ABOUT THE CLASS** -- pure-SSM and attention/SSM-hybrid have different binding costs. The pure-SSM null still stands for pure SSMs. ALSO REQUIRED FOR Falcon-H1: compute in bfloat16, NOT float16 -- fp16 overflows the SSM scan and yields all-NaN logits on prompts >=13 tokens (1/12 finite at fp16, 12/12 at bf16). TII's own docs: 'always use torch.bfloat16 instead of torch.float16'. Declare it per model as `compute_dtype` in the grid spec; storage stays f16. BUILD NOTE: no prebuilt wheels for cu130/torch2.11/py3.12, so both kernels compile from source. Use TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=8.0 MAX_JOBS=48 and --no-build-isolation (mamba-ssm's setup.py imports torch, which pip's isolated build env lacks). ~30 min on 128 cores. VERIFY IN USE, NOT MERELY INSTALLED: transformers falls back SILENTLY, so the check is that the log's 'fast path is not available' warning is ABSENT. ALSO PINS transformers==4.57.1 FOR ZAMBA2 -- see pin_reasons; the image's own 5.14.1 cannot load it at all, and the failure presents as a kernel problem.

pin_reasons.mamba-ssm: the fused selective-scan kernel. Installs ONLY with --no-build-isolation: its setup.py imports torch and pip's isolated build env has none. A finding that says 'install the kernels' without that is not runnable as written.
pin_reasons.causal-conv1d: the fused depthwise conv; same story
pin_reasons.transformers==4.57.1: ZAMBA2 WILL NOT LOAD ON transformers 5.x AND THE ERROR NAMES NEITHER THE VERSION NOR THE MODEL'S REAL PROBLEM. On 5.14.1 (what the vllm image ships, 2026-08-10) Zyphra/Zamba2-7B fails at load with `There is an issue with your definition of tie_weights_keys for ^layers.6.shared_transformer:...` -- a v5 weight-tying validation that Zamba2's config predates: it declares transformers_version 4.49.0.dev0. Pinning 4.57.1 loads it and it scores at 1.23 p/s. 4.57 is also the floor CLAUDE.md records for OLMo 3, so it is the highest version known to satisfy both. **AND THE KERNEL WARNING LIES ON A FAILED LOAD.** While Zamba2 was failing, the log carried 'The fast path is not available because one of (selective_state_update, selective_scan_fn, causal_conv1d_fn, causal_conv1d_update, mamba_inner_fn) is None' -- the very string this profile tells you to check for. The kernels were fine: all five entry points imported, is_mamba_ssm_available() and is_causal_conv1d_available() both returned True, and once a model actually loaded the warning was ABSENT. So a fast-path warning emitted DURING a failed load is not evidence about the kernels, and reading it as such sends you to rebuild kernels that work. Check it on a load that SUCCEEDED.

_bandwidth_note: min_inet_down_mbps IS A SELECTION CRITERION AND WE HAD NEVER FILTERED ON IT. Compute parallelises across GPUs; the network does not. Measured 2026-08-02 on the live offer board: a 4xGPU A100 box at $1.043/GPU -- IDENTICAL per-GPU price to a single -- was the SLOWEST option available, because its link is 624 Mbps and the roster is 1.42 TB. That is 5.1 h of download against 10.0 h of compute: the run goes from 10.0 h to 15.1 h and from $42 to $63, entirely on a field nobody was looking at. Both boxes used today passed this by luck (8.7 and 2.9 Gbps), not by filter.

dense.description: Cheapest 48GB-class card on a fast link, 150GB disk. NO gpu_name filter -- selection is by CAPABILITY (VRAM, link, disk), because the dense roster is one forward pass per prompt and the bill is DOWNLOAD. Peak disk is one model + margin: purge_model fires BEFORE each download and on every exit path including failure.

vllm022.description: Cheapest 48GB-class card on a CONTEMPORARY vLLM 0.22.1 IMAGE. For architectures vLLM SUPPORTED AND REMOVED: Aquila (until v0.24.0), Baichuan (until v0.23.0), jais. Pinning `vllm==0.22.1` onto the :latest image instead is an ABI CASCADE and does not work -- measured 12 Aug: transformers too new, then deep_ep compiled against another NCCL (undefined symbol ncclCommQueryProperties), then flashinfer-jit-cache mismatched against flashinfer, then a plan() TypeError, then EngineDeadError in step(). Four fixes got the model to LOAD and generation still died. The engine's own error names the last working version; take the image that shipped with it.

Check failed: (status == cudaSuccess)'. VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND is IGNORED in 0.22.1 (the log still reads 'Using FLASHINFER'), so there is no backend workaround; take an sm_80+ card.
